pr.title: Load only MariaDB Connector/C, and never write values into the SQL (1.4)
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 1.4, the last step of the SQL work: the server **loads only MariaDB Connector/C** and **never writes values into the SQL**.

> Stacked on #17 (MySQL prepared statements), which this PR targets. When #17 is merged, GitHub moves this PR to `master`.

## Changes

- **`MySQLInterface`**
  - Loads `libmariadb.dll` only. The fallback to Oracle's `libmysql.dll`, which administrators used to copy into `Bin` themselves, is gone: its `MYSQL_BIND` layout differs from the MariaDB headers `MySQLStatement` is compiled against.
  - `Load` now fails if the library lacks any function the server uses, and the error names the missing export, instead of the server failing on first use.
  - `IsMariaDB()` and `SupportsPreparedStatements()` are removed.
- **`MySQLConnection`**: always binds parameters, and applies its MariaDB TLS options unconditionally.
- **`SQLStatement::GenerateFromCommand`** is removed with its tests.
  - `DALConnection::Execute` and `DALRecordset::Open` now refuse a command with parameters on a client that cannot bind them; they never write the values into the SQL. No current client reaches that path: SQL Server via ADO, SQL CE, PostgreSQL and MySQL all bind.
  - The positional tests keep the one case the removed tests covered that still matters: names match as whole tokens (`@ID` never matches the start of `@IDX`), and `@@IDENTITY` and a lone `@` are left unchanged.
- **Docs**: the upgrade notes say a `libmysql.dll` left in `Bin` is no longer used and can be deleted. Setup leaves it alone, since hMailServer never installed it.

## Tests

No new regression test. The refuse path can't be reached with any client the server has, and the bound path is covered by `API.SqlValues` and the MySQL CI run from #17. The `SQLStatementTester` positional cases run through `Utilities.RunTestSuite`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Three places still build SQL from `SQLStatement::Escape` instead of parameters:
- `PersistentSecurityRange.cpp:244` (a `WHERE` on the range name);
- `PersistentIMAPFolder.cpp:230`;
- `PersistentRuleAction.cpp:143`.

The escaping there is correct, but moving them to parameters would let `Escape` go as well. I suggest a small separate PR.

commit.message:
Load only MariaDB Connector/C, and never write values into the SQL

The last step of the SQL work. Every database client binds command parameters
now, so the code that wrote the values into the SQL as escaped literals for a
client that could not is removed, and the client that needed it goes too.

- MySQLInterface loads libmariadb.dll only. It no longer falls back to Oracle's
  libmysql.dll, which an administrator once had to put in the Bin directory:
  its MYSQL_BIND is laid out differently from the MariaDB headers MySQLStatement
  is compiled against. Load now fails, naming the export, if the library lacks
  any function the server uses, rather than the server failing on first use.
- IsMariaDB and SupportsPreparedStatements are gone; MySQLConnection always
  binds, and applies its MariaDB TLS options unconditionally.
- SQLStatement::GenerateFromCommand is removed with its tests. DALConnection and
  DALRecordset refuse a command with parameters on a client that cannot bind
  them, instead of writing the values into the SQL - none does today.
- The positional parameter tests gain the whole-token case the removed tests
  covered: @ID never matches the start of @IDX, and @@IDENTITY and a lone @
  stay as they are.
- The upgrade notes say a libmysql.dll left in Bin is no longer used and can be
  deleted. The setup leaves it alone, since hMailServer never installed it.

No regression test is new: the refused path cannot be reached with any client
the server has, and API.SqlValues and the MySQL CI run cover the bound path.

issue.body:
## Summary

This is the follow-up from #19. It binds the last three values that were still written into the SQL text, then removes the escaping helpers. **After this PR, nothing in the server builds SQL from a value.**

## The three queries

| Query | Value | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| `PersistentSecurityRange::Exists` | The name of an auto-ban range: `"Auto-ban: " + user name` from failed logons | The client chooses the value. The escaping held, but it belongs in a parameter. |
| `PersistentIMAPFolder::GetExistsFolderContainingCharacter` | A new IMAP hierarchy delimiter, in `LIKE '%<char>%'` | **A bug on MySQL** (below) |
| `PersistentRuleAction::GetExistsFolderReferenceContainingCharacter` | The same, for rule actions' folders | Same bug |

**The MySQL bug:** a backslash was escaped to `'%\\%'`. MySQL then read the pattern's backslash as LIKE's default escape character, so a folder whose name contained `\` was never found. The delimiter could therefore be changed to `\` even though a folder already used it.

All three now bind their values. The LIKE checks bind a pattern made by the new `SQLStatement::EscapeLike`, with an explicit `ESCAPE '/'`. That is the form the greylisting query already uses, and every database reads it the same way.

## Removed

- `SQLStatement::Escape`, and `EscapeString` on `DALConnection` and its four implementations. Nothing called `EscapeString`.
- The escaping of raw columns (`NULL`, `current_timestamp`). These are SQL the server writes itself, now appended as they are rather than run through value escaping.

## Also

- `Property::WriteStringSetting_` wrote the setting's name into the SQL with `Formatter::Format("settingname = '{0}'")` and no escaping. The name is always one of the server's own, but it's now bound like the value, as the integer and boolean writes next to it already do.
- Many queries still build a `WHERE` clause with `Format("xid = %I64d", id)` (integer IDs), or append SQL the server writes itself (timestamps, IP comparisons). None of them can be injected, because no text value goes into them. Converting them to parameters is a Phase 5 cleanup, not a security fix.

## Tests

- `IMAP.HierarchyDelimiter.TestDelimiterChangeIsRefusedWhenAFolderContainsIt`: with a folder named `Back\slash`, changing the delimiter to `\` is refused, while a change to `/` goes through.
- `IMAP.HierarchyDelimiter.TestDelimiterChangeIsRefusedWhenARuleFolderContainsIt`: the same for a rule action's folder.
- `Security.AutoBan.TestIPRangeNameWithQuoteInUserName`: a user named `o'brien@example.test` is banned while a range with that name already exists. The new range must be named `... (1)`, which works only if `Exists` finds the name with the quote in it.
- `SQLStatementTester`: `EscapeLike`.

On the old code, the two delimiter tests are expected to fail on MySQL, for the reason above, and pass on the other databases.
